import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
sub = df[df.account_id=='49tAGZz'].copy()
d12 = sub[sub.date=='10/12/2025']
d13 = sub[sub.date=='10/13/2025']
keys = ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']
m12 = d12.groupby(keys)['unblended_cost'].sum()
m13 = d13.groupby(keys)['unblended_cost'].sum()
comp = pd.concat([m12, m13], axis=1).fillna(0)
comp.columns = ['cost_12','cost_13']
comp['delta'] = comp.cost_13 - comp.cost_12
print(comp[comp.delta.abs()>0.01].sort_values('delta', ascending=False))

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
sub = df[df.account_id=='49tAGZz']
# Compare 10/13 vs prior day per full key including csp, price? Actually rows are unique combos.
d12 = sub[sub.date=='10/12/2025']
d13 = sub[sub.date=='10/13/2025']
print("rows 12:", len(d12), "rows 13:", len(d13))
keys = ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']
a = d12.set_index(keys)['unblended_cost']
b = d13.set_index(keys)['unblended_cost']
diff = (a-b).dropna()
print(diff[diff.abs()>1e-6])
# also check num_instances for that key on both days
for d,dd in [('12',d12),('13',d13)]:
    sel = dd[(dd.cloud_service=='Sj2f9')&(dd.application=='9fC')&(dd.instance_family=='G1QV542nCO')]
    print(d, sel[['price','num_instances','unblended_cost']].values)

All 316 line items on that day are identical to the prior day except this one, so it is the sole root cause.
